blocks.text: Church, Elijah had just come down off Mount Carmel. He had called on the LORD, and fire fell from heaven in front of everybody. It was the biggest day of his life. And then the queen heard about it.

verses.text: And Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and withal how he had slain all the prophets with the sword.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The same man who stood up to four hundred and fifty false prophets is sitting under a tree, asking God to let him die. Tired. Scared. Alone. Sure he had failed.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Some of y'all know that tree. You have been that tired. And look at what God did. He did not fuss at Elijah. He did not preach him a sermon.

verses.text: And as he lay and slept under a juniper tree, behold, then an angel touched him, and said unto him, Arise and eat.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Warm bread off the coals. A jar of water. A gentle touch. And then God let him sleep some more, and did it all again. God knew the journey was too much for him, and he took care of his body first.

verses.text: And he arose, and did eat and drink, and went in the strength of that meat forty days and forty nights unto Horeb the mount of God.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: God did not leave him in that cave. He gave him rest, then a quiet word, then a job to do. And he told him he was not the only one after all. There were seven thousand in Israel who had not bowed to Baal.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Church, we look for God in the wind and the fire. Sometimes he comes in the quiet, after the noise is gone. And sometimes the holiest thing for a weary soul is a meal and a good night's sleep. If you are sitting under that tree tonight, do not sit there by yourself. Call somebody who loves you.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to 1 Kings 19:1-15 (450 prophets 18:22, 7,000 v18); Elijah's wish to die told gently; ends pointing a weary listener to someone who loves her; no outcome promised.

cultural.note: 'Arise and eat' at the turn; 'y'all' once, natural speech; despair never shamed.
